Yes. Multiple lines of fossil evidence indicate that flowering plants (angiosperms) existed before or during the Mesozoic Era, which is the age of dinosaurs [d3,d1]. A 260-million-year-old flower fossil from the Permian predates the first dinosaurs [d3]. By the Early Cretaceous (~140 Ma) and throughout the Cretaceous, angiosperm fossils and pollen are well documented alongside dinosaurs [d1,d4,d5,d8]. Some sources also describe fragrant flowers from ~100 Ma in the Cretaceous, coeval with dinosaur abundance [d6]. Thus, flowers did exist during the age of dinosaurs.
